decks.notes: This deck focuses on quickly generating a large amount of mana and utilizing spells that can generate additional copies or allow for extra turns to build up a powerful Storm count. By chaining together a series of spells and rituals, the deck aims to eventually cast Tendrils of Agony to deal lethal damage to the opponent. The deck includes a mix of fast mana acceleration, tutors, disruption, and card draw to enable the combo and protect it from opposing interaction. The key is to carefully sequence spells and manage resources to set up a winning Storm turn.

This deck focuses on using control elements like counterspells, removal, and disruption to maintain a strong defensive position while setting up card advantage and filtering through the deck to find key cards. The inclusion of Companion Lurrus of the Dream-Den allows for additional value by casting cheap permanents from the graveyard. The deck also includes efficient creatures like Psychic Frog and Orcish Bowmasters to provide additional threats and utility. Overall, the deck aims to outlast opponents while steadily advancing its game plan to ultimately secure victory.

This Vintage Doomsday combo deck focuses on quickly assembling the key cards needed to win the game, utilizing powerful draw spells and counterspells to protect the combo. The goal is to set up a Doomsday pile that will allow you to win the game by either casting Thassa's Oracle or using Lórien Revealed to exile your opponent's library. The deck also includes disruptive elements like Force of Will and Flusterstorm to control the game and protect your combo. With careful planning and timing, this deck can be a highly effective and explosive combo deck in the Vintage format.

The deck focuses on assembling a powerful board state quickly with mana acceleration and artifact synergy, combining aggressive creatures with powerful artifact cards like Karn, the Great Creator and Mystic Forge. The goal is to disrupt the opponent's game plan with cards like Chalice of the Void and Lodestone Golem, while generating card advantage and manipulating the top of the deck with Sensei's Divining Top. The win condition is to overwhelm the opponent with resilient threats like Glaring Fleshraker and Nettlecyst, backed up by cards that allow for combo finishes like Time Vault and The One Ring.

This Esper Control deck focuses on disrupting the opponent's strategy with counterspells, removal, and disruptive cards like Lavinia, Azorius Renegade and Null Rod. It also utilizes card advantage with Ancestral Recall, Dig Through Time, and Treasure Cruise. The deck aims to control the game through efficient removal and card advantage while utilizing powerful mana acceleration such as Black Lotus and Urza's Saga. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion allows for additional value and recursion of key permanents.

The main concept of this Vintage 1 vs 1 Aggro - Hatebear deck is to disrupt and slow down the opponent's game plan by playing powerful hate cards like Void Mirror and Archon of Emeria while also deploying aggressive creatures like Anointed Peacekeeper and Clarion Conqueror to apply early pressure. The deck aims to control the game through disruptive spells and hate creatures while also utilizing mana acceleration from cards like Chrome Mox and the Moxen to quickly establish a strong board presence and close out games swiftly.

The deck focuses on disrupting opponents with hatebears while aggressively pushing the tempo with efficient creatures. Using cards like Archon of Emeria and Chancellor of the Annex to slow down opponents, the deck aims to control the game and overwhelm the opponent with its efficient threats like Clarion Conqueror and White Plume Adventurer. With a mix of disruptive hate cards like Chalice of the Void and Void Mirror, the deck is designed to disrupt and pressure opponents, making it a challenging matchup for many decks in the Vintage format.

The main concept of this deck is to disrupt your opponent's strategy with hatebears while applying pressure with aggressive creatures. By utilizing cards like Void Mirror and Archon of Emeria, you can slow down your opponent's spells and disrupt their mana base. Anointed Peacekeeper and Clarion Conqueror provide additional hate against specific strategies. The deck also includes mana acceleration with cards like Chrome Mox and Ancient Tomb to quickly deploy your threats. Overall, the deck aims to control the game by limiting your opponent's options while maintaining a strong board presence.

This Vintage Combo - Storm deck focuses on quickly generating mana through powerful mana accelerators such as Moxen, Black Lotus, and Sol Ring, allowing for explosive plays. The deck aims to generate a large storm count using spells like Dark Ritual and Paradoxical Outcome before finishing the opponent off with Tendrils of Agony. It also includes key cards like Time Walk for extra turns, Tinker to search for powerful artifacts like Bolas's Citadel, and Yawgmoth's Will to recur spells from the graveyard. The deck is packed with powerful draw and disruption spells to ensure its combo goes off smoothly.

This deck focuses on disrupting the opponent's game plan by playing hatebears such as Archon of Emeria and Chancellor of the Annex while also using cards like Trinisphere and Void Mirror to slow down their spells. The aggro strategy is supported by creatures like Anointed Peacekeeper and Clarion Conqueror, aiming to put pressure on the opponent while controlling the board. The deck utilizes fast mana like Black Lotus and Moxen to accelerate its game plan and take advantage of powerful cards like Karakas and White Plume Adventurer.

The deck focuses on controlling the game through a combination of counterspells, removal, and card advantage, utilizing powerful vintage staples and efficient interaction to disrupt the opponent's game plan while setting up its own win conditions. Additionally, the inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion provides added value by allowing for recursion of key threats and resources from the graveyard. The deck aims to outlast the opponent and grind out incremental advantages until it can secure a decisive victory.

The deck focuses on disrupting the opponent's strategy with hatebears like Anointed Peacekeeper, Archon of Emeria, and Chancellor of the Annex, while also applying pressure with aggro creatures like Clarion Conqueror and White Plume Adventurer. It includes cards like Void Mirror and Cavern of Souls to further disrupt the opponent's spells. The deck also includes mana acceleration with cards like the Mox cycle and Ancient Tomb to quickly deploy threats. The goal is to control the game through disruptive creatures and spell denial while maintaining a strong aggressive presence.

This deck focuses on utilizing fast mana and card advantage to control the game while deploying threats to quickly close out the game. It aims to disrupt the opponent's game plan with counterspells and removal spells while leveraging the power of cards like Ancestral Recall and Dig Through Time to draw into more resources. The presence of companion Lurrus of the Dream-Den gives the deck additional resilience and flexibility, allowing it to play a longer game if necessary. The deck's primary objective is to apply pressure early and efficiently while maintaining a grip on the game through disruption and card advantage.

This deck focuses on quickly filling up the graveyard with cards like Golgari Thug and Stinkweed Imp, using Bazaar of Baghdad and Serum Powder to effectively dig through the deck. It aims to reanimate powerful creatures like Ichorid and Prized Amalgam, creating a overwhelming board presence with cards like Creeping Chill. The goal is to overwhelm the opponent with a combination of fast plays and graveyard recursion, while also containing disruptive elements like Force of Will and Chalice of the Void to protect the combo.

This deck aims to disrupt the opponent's strategy while building up a board presence with aggressive creatures. The hatebears like Archon of Emeria and Anointed Peacekeeper slow down the opponent's spells and attacks, while cards like Chalice of the Void and Void Mirror restrict their options even further. The deck also has a card advantage engine with Witch Enchanter and Seasoned Dungeoneer, as well as a backup win condition with Clarion Conqueror. The efficient mana base and fast mana acceleration from cards like Chrome Mox and the Moxen allow for explosive starts and consistent pressure on the opponent.

The main concept of this deck is to utilize the graveyard as a resource to quickly fill the board with powerful creatures like Narcomoeba, Golgari Thug, and Ichorid. By using cards like Bazaar of Baghdad and Noxious Revival, the player can easily discard cards to trigger abilities and bring back creatures from the graveyard. The Combo - Dredge archetype focuses on quickly overwhelming the opponent with a relentless stream of creatures and leveraging their graveyard interactions to maintain tempo and pressure throughout the game.
